stem: In Nagarjuna's Mulamadhyamakakarika (24.18), the root text of the Madhyamaka school, dependent arising is said to be the same as what?
options: mind-only (cittamatra)
emptiness (shunyata)
true suchness (tathata)
storehouse mind (alaya)
why: In chapter 24, verse 18, Nagarjuna says that whatever arises dependently is what is called emptiness; it is a dependent designation, and it is the middle way. Mulamadhyamakakarika 24.18.

es.stem: En el Mulamadhyamakakarika de Nagarjuna (24.18), el texto raíz de la escuela Madhyamaka, ¿con qué se identifica el surgimiento dependiente?
options: solo mente (cittamatra)
la vacuidad (shunyata)
la talidad (tathata)
la mente almacén (alaya)
es.why: En el capítulo 24, verso 18, Nagarjuna dice que todo lo que surge de forma dependiente es lo que se llama vacuidad; es una designación dependiente, y es el camino medio. Mulamadhyamakakarika 24.18.

stem: Buddhaghosa's Visuddhimagga (Path of Purification), the great Theravada manual, is built around which three trainings, in order?
options: generosity, virtue and meditation
faith, effort and mindfulness
virtue, concentration and wisdom
right view, intention and speech
why: The Visuddhimagga opens with the Buddha's verse on untangling the tangle (Samyutta Nikaya 1.23) and arranges the whole path under virtue (sila), concentration (samadhi) and wisdom (panna).

es.stem: El Visuddhimagga (Camino de purificación) de Buddhaghosa, el gran manual theravada, se organiza en torno a ¿qué tres entrenamientos, en orden?
options: generosidad, virtud y meditación
fe, esfuerzo y atención plena
virtud, concentración y sabiduría
recta visión, intención y habla
es.why: El Visuddhimagga empieza con el verso del Buda sobre desenredar la maraña (Samyutta Nikaya 1.23) y ordena todo el camino bajo virtud (sila), concentración (samadhi) y sabiduría (panna).

stem: In the Indian and Tibetan Mahayana tradition, which work is Shantideva, the monk of Nalanda, remembered for composing?
options: the Bodhicharyavatara
the Abhidharma Treasury
the Lamp for the Path
the Precious Garland
why: Shantideva, an eighth-century monk of Nalanda, is credited with the Bodhicharyavatara, the Way of the Bodhisattva. The Abhidharmakosha (Treasury of Abhidharma) is Vasubandhu's, the Lamp for the Path is Atisha's, and the Precious Garland (Ratnavali) is Nagarjuna's.
source: Shantideva, Bodhicharyavatara; Buton, History of Buddhism

es.stem: En la tradición mahayana india y tibetana, ¿qué obra se recuerda que compuso Shantideva, el monje de Nalanda?
options: el Bodhicharyavatara
el Tesoro del Abhidharma
la Lámpara para el camino
la Guirnalda preciosa
es.why: A Shantideva, monje de Nalanda del siglo VIII, se le atribuye el Bodhicharyavatara, el Camino del bodhisattva. El Abhidharmakosha (Tesoro del Abhidharma) es de Vasubandhu, la Lámpara para el camino es de Atisha y la Guirnalda preciosa (Ratnavali) es de Nagarjuna.

stem: In the Chan records, when the monk Damei ("Great Plum") hears that Mazu now teaches "no mind, no Buddha", why does Mazu then say "the plum is ripe"?
options: Damei gave up his old words for Mazu's new ones
Damei held to "this mind is Buddha", unshaken
Damei left his mountain to rejoin Mazu's hall
Damei sent Mazu a gift of plums from the hill
why: Told of Mazu's new saying, Damei answers that the old man can confuse people as he likes; for him, this very mind is Buddha. Mazu hears and says the plum is ripe: Damei's insight is his own. Jingde Chuandeng Lu, Damei Fachang.
source: Jingde Chuandeng Lu (Transmission of the Lamp), entry on Damei Fachang

es.stem: En los registros chan, cuando el monje Damei ("Gran Ciruelo") oye que Mazu ahora enseña "ni mente ni Buda", ¿por qué Mazu dice entonces "el ciruelo está maduro"?
options: Damei cambió sus viejas palabras por las nuevas de Mazu
Damei se mantuvo en "esta mente es Buda", sin vacilar
Damei dejó su montaña para volver a la sala de Mazu
Damei le mandó a Mazu un regalo de ciruelas del monte
es.why: Cuando le cuentan el nuevo dicho de Mazu, Damei responde que el viejo puede confundir a la gente cuanto quiera; para él, esta misma mente es Buda. Mazu lo oye y dice que el ciruelo está maduro: la comprensión de Damei es propia. Jingde Chuandeng Lu, Damei Fachang.

stem: A Soto Zen monastery must choose its tenzo (head cook). Following Dogen's Tenzo Kyokun (Instructions for the Cook), who should hold the post?
options: a lay servant hired for skill at the stove
the newest novice, as training in humility
the monk who struggles most in zazen
a senior monk with a mind set on the Way
why: Dogen says the tenzo post has always been given to accomplished monks with way-seeking mind, because cooking for the community is itself practice; the old cook he met in China was a senior monk. Dogen, Tenzo Kyokun.

es.stem: Un monasterio zen soto debe elegir a su tenzo (cocinero principal). Según el Tenzo Kyokun (Instrucciones para el cocinero) de Dogen, ¿quién debe ocupar el puesto?
options: un sirviente laico contratado por su oficio
el novicio más nuevo, para aprender humildad
el monje al que más le cuesta el zazen
un monje veterano con la mente en el Camino
es.why: Dogen dice que el puesto de tenzo siempre se ha dado a monjes avanzados con mente que busca el Camino, porque cocinar para la comunidad es en sí práctica; el viejo cocinero que conoció en China era un monje veterano. Dogen, Tenzo Kyokun.

stem: In the Pali Vinaya's Cullavagga, what does it mean when the sangha formally turns its bowls down (patta nikkujjana) toward a layperson?
options: he is barred from taking refuge for life
the monks will fast until he says sorry
he must ordain as a novice for one season
monks will not take his alms or visit him
why: The Cullavagga lets the sangha turn the bowl down toward a layman who, for example, falsely accuses a monk: monks then do not visit his home or accept his offerings. It is lifted when he makes amends. Vinaya, Cullavagga V.20.

es.stem: En el Cullavagga del Vinaya pali, ¿qué significa que la sangha vuelva formalmente sus cuencos boca abajo (patta nikkujjana) hacia un laico?
options: le prohíben tomar refugio de por vida
los monjes ayunan hasta que se disculpe
debe ordenarse de novicio por una temporada
no aceptarán sus ofrendas ni lo visitarán
es.why: El Cullavagga permite a la sangha volver el cuenco boca abajo hacia un laico que, por ejemplo, acusa falsamente a un monje: los monjes no visitan su casa ni aceptan sus ofrendas. Se levanta cuando él repara el daño. Vinaya, Cullavagga V.20.

stem: in Nagarjuna's Mulamadhyamakakarika (chapter 24), what are the two truths, and why does he say the teaching needs both?
why: Nagarjuna says the Buddhas teach the Dharma relying on two truths, conventional and ultimate; without relying on the conventional the ultimate cannot be taught, and without understanding the ultimate nirvana is not reached. Madhyamaka schools, especially in Tibet, debate exactly how the two relate.

rubric.point: conventional truth: the everyday world of things, names and agreed usage, in which teaching, ethics and practice happen. calling it simply "a lie" or "an illusion to throw away" does not count.
ultimate truth: emptiness, that nothing exists on its own, independent of causes, conditions and names. "nothing exists at all" does not count.

why both: the ultimate can only be taught by relying on the conventional, and without understanding the ultimate, nirvana is not reached (24.10). saying only "both are true" with no reason is partly met.
mentions the warning that emptiness wrongly grasped is like a snake seized the wrong way (24.11), or that Madhyamaka schools read the relation of the two truths differently.

es.stem: en el Mulamadhyamakakarika de Nagarjuna (capítulo 24), ¿cuáles son las dos verdades, y por qué dice que la enseñanza necesita ambas?
es.why: Nagarjuna dice que los budas enseñan el Dharma apoyándose en dos verdades, la convencional y la última; sin apoyarse en la convencional no se puede enseñar la última, y sin comprender la última no se alcanza el nirvana. Las escuelas madhyamaka, sobre todo en el Tíbet, debaten cómo se relacionan exactamente.

stem: in the Padhana Sutta (Sutta Nipata 3.2), what is Mara's "army" that comes against the striving Bodhisatta, and how does he say he will defeat it?
why: In the Padhana Sutta the Bodhisatta names Mara's ten troops: sensual desire, discontent, hunger and thirst, craving, sloth and torpor, fear, doubt, hypocrisy and obstinacy, gain, fame and honor, and self-praise with contempt for others. He says he will break it with wisdom, as a stone breaks an unbaked pot. Sutta Nipata 3.2.

rubric.point: says Mara's army is made of inner states or defilements, not outside soldiers, and names at least two of the troops (for example desire, discontent, hunger and thirst, craving, sloth, fear, doubt, hypocrisy, gain and fame, self-praise). naming none is partly met if the inner-states point is clear.
says the Bodhisatta defeats it by wisdom or clear seeing (like a stone breaking an unbaked clay pot), not by force or by giving in. "by fighting hard" alone does not count.
mentions that Mara first comes kindly, urging him to give up striving and live, or that Mara finally gives up and his lute slips from his arm.

es.stem: en el Padhana Sutta (Sutta Nipata 3.2), ¿qué es el "ejército" de Mara que viene contra el Bodhisatta que se esfuerza, y cómo dice él que lo vencerá?
es.why: En el Padhana Sutta el Bodhisatta nombra las diez tropas de Mara: el deseo sensual, el descontento, el hambre y la sed, el ansia, la pereza y el sopor, el miedo, la duda, la hipocresía y la obstinación, la ganancia, la fama y los honores, y el elogio propio con desprecio de los demás. Dice que lo romperá con sabiduría, como una piedra rompe una vasija sin cocer. Sutta Nipata 3.2.
